Addressed in 08fd00f9962ad77a38c2f9d2eab9d8c4772f8ac5.

Analysis: The stable semantic convention task still runs `maybeStablePeerService()` assertions. Without the `service.peer` opt-in, those assertions only select the legacy key. Restoring the opt-in in both the JVM argument and metadata configuration makes the stable task exercise `service.peer.name` and keeps metadata collection aligned with the test mode.

Downsides: The stable task tests the database and service-peer semantic convention domains together instead of isolating them.

replies.body:
Addressed in ec3bd9de5bdbe348327d33f4da7a183cf9e4d7c9.

Analysis: The existing test called `renewSlotCache` directly and only checked `CLUSTER` spans. It did not run the normal cluster connection lookup. Calling `JedisCluster.set` and `get` exercises the `getConnection*` advice. threads.body:
[General] When `setHost` or `setPort` changes a previously captured connection to an unrepresentable endpoint, `target` is `null` and this guard leaves the old virtual-field value in place. Stable telemetry then reports the stale address; clear the field by setting the nullable result unconditionally.

This issue also appears on line 99 of the same file.

replies.body:
Addressed in 81e9ad4123555a336dcb4c7e6d17b74659ffaff6.

Analysis: `captureConnectionTarget` kept the old virtual-field value when `RedisServerTarget.ofHostAndPort` returned null. Setting null removes virtual-field state, so the method now always writes its computed result. A unit test covers invalid host and port updates.

Upsides: Stable telemetry no longer reports a stale server target after mutable Jedis connections receive invalid endpoint values.

Downsides: This adds one virtual-field set when no target can be represented. Setting null only clears existing state.

threads.body: [General] A null aggregate target currently means “do not install a context.” During sharded, cluster, or Sentinel initialization, connection constructors then use their individual host/port fallback, so a client with one unrepresentable configured endpoint can still report a selected endpoint instead of omitting `server.address` as required. Carry an explicit “configured but unavailable” marker and make target capture/lookup suppress the direct fallback while that marker is current.

replies.body:
Addressed in b53dfffe2f63123eff8ef0070f386b4f6614f047.

Analysis: A nullable target could not distinguish an aggregate client with an unrepresentable configuration from a direct client with no aggregate target. `ConfiguredTarget` now preserves that distinction in the current context and pool virtual field. Connection capture and lookup honor the marker, while ordinary pools still allow direct host and port capture.

Upsides: Sharded, cluster, and Sentinel clients now omit the stable server target when their aggregate configuration cannot be represented. Tests cover current-context and pooled marker propagation.

Downsides: Creating configured target contexts now allocates a small holder for the nullable target.

threads.body: [General] This wrapper inherits `ofUnorderedEndpointsAndLogicalName`'s logical-name fallback: an empty Sentinel set, or a set where every endpoint is unrepresentable, returns `masterName` alone. That contradicts this PR's fail-closed contract that an unavailable configured endpoint list must omit the target (the shared fallback is explicitly covered in `RedisServerTargetTest.java:109-115`). Validate the endpoint list before invoking the permissive discovery helper.

replies.body:
Addressed in 67bbf56f670cf4a27b005e25305511b754d979cf.

Analysis: `ofSentinels` passed its endpoint list directly to a helper that permits logical-name-only discovery targets. It now requires the same endpoint list to produce a strict unordered target before it adds the Sentinel master name.

Upsides: Empty and wholly unrepresentable Sentinel endpoint lists now fail closed instead of reporting only the master name. Tests cover both cases.

Downsides: Valid Sentinel endpoint lists are parsed twice during client initialization.

threads.body: [Testing] `getResource()` runs before the `try`, so a borrow failure after the Sentinel pool has started its listener threads skips `destroy()` and leaks the pool. Use an outer `try/finally` around both borrowing and using the resource so pool cleanup also occurs on borrow or resource-close failures.

replies.body:
Addressed in c0767ea32fa1b0aeb63ff0aafe0aa7e110595d12.

Analysis: Nested finally blocks make pool.destroy() run when getResource(), set(), or close() throws.

Upsides: The test no longer leaks Sentinel listener threads after a failed resource borrow or close.

Downsides: The test has one additional nested try/finally block.

threads.body: [Build] Direct tests of javaagent helpers should live in a `JvmTestSuite` named `unitTests` in the javaagent project (`src/unitTests`) rather than a separate `javaagent-unit-tests` subproject. This adds a non-standard project and duplicates its classpath/task wiring; move these tests and dependencies into the existing javaagent build and remove this include.

replies.body:
Addressed in cd731d822a041cfa21f87c6e181b8c4ad7a57667.

Analysis: The repository's javaagent test convention gives a unitTests suite direct access to helper classes without installing the agent. Moving the tests there removes the separate project's duplicate classpath and task setup while preserving its dependencies and database semconv setting.

Upsides: The tests now follow the repository convention, run from the javaagent check lifecycle, and keep their direct helper access.

Downsides: The test task path changes from :instrumentation:jedis:jedis-2.0:javaagent-unit-tests:test to :instrumentation:jedis:jedis-2.0:javaagent:unitTests.

threads.body: [General] The configured context only covers the `borrowObject()` call, so a previously created idle resource keeps whatever target its `Connection` constructor captured. For example, Jedis 2.x exposes `Pool.addObjects(int)` (and Commons Pool can replenish `minIdle` in its evictor thread); those connections are created outside this scope and therefore retain the selected master/node target. Borrowing one then closes this scope before the command runs, causing Sentinel or cluster telemetry to report that selected endpoint instead of the configured aggregate target. Stamp the returned `Jedis` connection with the pool target before closing the scope (and add a pre-created-idle-resource regression test).

replies.body:
Addressed in b8e01a807922ae5cd57e7e88ee2fc64adf4fb4fd.

Analysis: A pooled Jedis connection can be created before the configured pool target becomes current. The getResource exit advice now replaces that stale connection target while the pool context is still current, then closes the scope in a finally block. The regression test pre-creates an idle Sentinel resource before borrowing it.

Upsides: Stable telemetry keeps the configured aggregate target for idle resources created by callers or pool maintenance threads.

Downsides: Stable configured-target pool borrows now perform one additional type check and virtual-field write.
